summary: This unit teaches you to provide reception services at a villa or small property: preparing the desk, welcoming and checking in guests, checking ID, taking payment, allocating rooms and keys, handling messages, safe deposit boxes and wake-up calls, solving problems, checking guests out, and keeping guests, records and the property safe.

blocks.p: This unit covers the work of the reception (front desk) agent at a villa or small property, from the moment you start your shift to the moment you hand over to the next one. You prepare the desk, welcome guests, check them in, give them a key and the information they need, look after their messages and requests, check them out and keep the records. It is for HOSPITALITY VILLA/PROPERTIES SERVICES LEVEL 2 trainees.

Reception is the **heart of the property**. The guest meets you first and last, and what you do in those minutes shapes how they remember the whole stay. A warm welcome and accurate work earn good reviews; a careless one loses guests. Reception is also the guests' **security**: you control the keys, the room numbers and the information about who is staying.

blocks.note: How you are assessed: two theory papers (multiple-choice questions, short answers and essays) and two practical tasks in the Centre's training room. In the first you prepare the desk and check in several kinds of guest, including a walk-in and an early arrival. In the second you run a reception shift with calls, messages, keys, a wake-up call, the safe deposit box and a check-out with a mixed J$ and US$ payment. The assessor watches your manner, accuracy, privacy and records.

blocks.label: Tip

sections.title: Preparing for the shift and the reception desk

blocks.p: A good shift begins before the first guest arrives. Arrive on time, in a clean uniform with your name badge, with your hair, nails and shoes tidy. Then prepare the desk.

ol: Read the **log book and the handover notes** from the last shift: what is still to do, what went wrong, what guests are waiting for.
Check the **arrivals list** (who comes today, when, with what requests) and the **departures list**.
Check the **room status report** with housekeeping: which rooms are ready, which are dirty and which are out of order.
Count the **float** with a supervisor and sign for it.
Check that you have **forms, pens, key cards, key folders, receipts, brochures and maps**.
Check that the computer, printer, phone and card machine work; report any fault.
Check the **message light** and the voicemail for messages left overnight.
Make sure the desk is clean and tidy, with no guest papers left in view.

blocks.note: Never leave the cash or the keys unattended. Lock the float in the drawer or the safe whenever you leave the desk, even for a minute.
blocks.label: Safety

head: Word
Meaning
rows: Arrivals list
The guests due to arrive on the day
Departures list
The guests due to leave on the day
In-house list
Every guest staying tonight
Room status report
A report that shows whether each room is occupied, vacant, clean, dirty or out of order
Float
The fixed amount of cash a cashier starts with, to give change
Folio
The guest's bill, showing charges and payments
ETA, ETD
Estimated time of arrival, estimated time of departure
No-show
A guest with a booking who neither arrives nor cancels
Walk-in
A guest who arrives with no booking

ul: Stand or sit upright at the desk. Do not lean, eat, chew gum or use your own phone.
Smile and make eye contact. Use the guest's name once you know it.
Speak clearly, in plain words, with a warm tone. Use 'Good morning', 'Please', 'Thank you' and 'My pleasure'.
Do not argue with a guest, and do not complain about colleagues or the property in front of guests.

blocks.note: Team Jamaica is the customer service training for people who work with visitors; it is run by the Tourism Product Development Company (TPDCo). Its message is simple: welcome every visitor warmly, and make them feel safe.
blocks.label: Jamaica

ul: Greet each guest at once, with a smile, eye contact and a warm welcome: 'Good afternoon, welcome to Cedar Hill Villa.'
If you are on the phone or busy, **smile and nod** so the guest knows you will help soon, and finish the call quickly.
If a guest is waiting, say 'I will be with you in just a moment' and keep the promise.

flow: Greet the guest warmly
Ask for the name and find the booking
Confirm dates, room, rate and number of guests
Check photo ID
Guest completes and signs the registration card
Set up payment and give a receipt
Choose a ready room and issue keys privately
Explain the facilities and update the system

blocks.p: When a guest says 'I have a booking', ask for the **name** and look for the booking. Confirm the **dates, room type, rate, meal plan and number of guests**. Check special requests (a cot, a late meal, a birthday). If the name is not on the list, check the spelling, the booker's name and the date. If there is still no booking, treat the guest as a walk-in only after you have checked with the manager or reservations.

Every guest signs a **registration card** or form. It records who is staying and agrees the property's terms. It usually shows: full name, home address, nationality, passport or ID number, phone number and email, arrival and departure dates, vehicle registration if any, method of payment and signature. Check that it is complete and legible, that the signature matches the ID, and that you have the details of **each adult** if the property's policy requires it.

head: Guest
Usual ID
Check
rows: Visitor from overseas
Passport
Name, photo, nationality and expiry date; the visa or arrival stamp if the policy needs it
Jamaican resident
Driver's licence, national ID, passport or voter ID card, as the property's policy allows
Name, photo and expiry date match the booking and the card
Child
Passport or birth certificate, as the policy states
Names of the adult responsible for the child

ul: Ask politely: 'May I see your passport, please? I need it to complete your registration.'
Look at the **photo**, name and expiry date. Check that the ID belongs to the guest.
Copy or record only what the policy needs, then **hand the ID back at once**.
Never keep a guest's passport overnight unless the law or the property's policy requires it and you have the guest's agreement. Store it securely if you do.

blocks.note: ID checks are for the guest's own safety and the property's. They stop fraud, prevent the wrong person from getting keys or account information, and help in an emergency.
blocks.label: Remember

blocks.p: Ask how the guest will pay: card, cash, bank transfer or a booking already paid by an agent. Explain any **deposit** or **pre-authorisation** (a hold placed on the guest's card to cover the stay and extras; it is released when the guest leaves). If the guest pays a cash deposit, **count the cash in front of the guest, record it and give a receipt**. Use only the property's own rate for the day when you change US$ or J$.

head: Payment method
What to do
rows: Card
Check the name on the card matches the guest. Use the card machine; give the guest the slip and keep the card details secure.
Cash in J$ or US$
Count it twice, record it, give a receipt, lock it in the float or safe, and hand it in as the policy says.
Booking paid by an agent or company
Check what is paid and what the guest must pay (extras); record it on the folio.
Walk-in guest
Ask for payment in advance or a pre-authorisation, because there is no earlier booking to secure the stay.

blocks.p: **Worked example (made-up figures for practice only).** A guest pays a deposit of US$200 in cash. The property's rate for the day is US$1 = J$155. The deposit is 200 x 155 = **J$31,000**. Write the amount in both currencies on the receipt.

blocks.note: Counterfeit notes are a risk. Follow the property's way of checking large notes, and refer anything doubtful to your supervisor. Never accuse the guest in public.
blocks.label: Safety

head: Status
Meaning
rows: Occupied
A guest is staying in the room
Vacant dirty
The guest has left; the room is not yet cleaned
Vacant clean
Cleaned, but not yet checked by the supervisor
Vacant clean, inspected
Cleaned and checked: ready for a new guest
Out of order
Not available because of a fault, such as a leak or a broken air conditioner
Do not disturb (DND)
The guest does not want visitors or cleaning
On change
The guest has left; the room is being cleaned and prepared

blocks.p: Only a room that is **vacant clean and inspected** may be given to a guest. When a guest checks out, tell housekeeping at once so that the room can be cleaned and sold again. If a room has a fault, tell maintenance and mark it out of order.

ul: Give the room type the guest booked, or a better one only if the manager agrees (an **upgrade**).
Match special requests: ground floor for a guest who cannot climb stairs, a quiet room for a light sleeper, connecting rooms for a family.
Do not give a room that has not been inspected, or one still marked dirty.
Do not promise a view or a floor that the policy does not guarantee.

blocks.h: When the room is not ready

ul: Apologise, give an honest time, and offer facilities while the guest waits: a seat in the lobby, a cold drink or a short walk around the grounds.
Finish the registration, ID and payment in advance so the key is ready at once.
Tag the luggage and store it securely, with the bell staff.
Ask housekeeping to make the room a priority. Phone the guest or send the bell attendant when it is ready, and write it in the log.

blocks.h: When there is no room: overbooking

blocks.p: If a guest with a **guaranteed** booking arrives and the property is full, the manager arranges a room of at least the same standard at another property. This is called **walking** the guest. The property usually pays for the room and transport (check your property's policy), and brings the guest back when a room is free. Apologise sincerely and let the manager lead. Never argue with the guest or blame reservations.

flow: Greet and find out how many people and nights
Check which rooms are free and clean
Quote the rate with meals, currency and tax
Check ID and complete the registration card
Take payment in advance or pre-authorise
Open the account and issue keys privately
Explain the facilities

ul: **Never say the room number aloud.** Write it on the key folder and turn the folder so only the guest sees it.
Give the guest only the keys for their own room. Count the keys or cards you issue and record it.
If a guest says they have lost a key: **check ID against the registration first**, then make a new key and **cancel the old one** so that it no longer works.
Keep **master keys** locked, count them at each shift and sign them out. Only authorised staff may use them.
Never let a stranger into a room, even if they say they are the guest's friend or family.

blocks.note: A key card is useless once cancelled, but a metal key can be copied. If a metal key is lost, tell the manager; the lock may need to be changed.
blocks.label: Safety

sections.title: Information, messages, mail, wake-up calls and safes

blocks.p: Guests ask about meal times, the Wi-Fi password, the pool rules, the safe, beaches, shops, restaurants, tours and transport. Learn the property's facts before the shift, and keep a **facilities card**, a map and the list of local places beside the desk. If you do not know an answer, say 'Let me find out for you', and find out. Never guess. Give directions clearly, use a map, and offer a licensed taxi if the place is far. Explain the **check-out time**, the safe and the emergency exits at check-in.

blocks.h: Taking a message for a guest

ol: Do not say whether the guest is staying or give the room number. Say, 'I can take a message for you.'
Write down the **guest's name, the caller's name and number, the message, the date, the time and your own name**.
Read the message back to the caller.
Record it, and switch on the message light on the room phone if the property has one.
Put the message in a sealed, named envelope.
Pass it to the guest privately, as soon as possible, and switch the light off afterwards.

blocks.note: Calls from the telephone operator or a caller who asks for a guest by room number: put the call through without saying the number, or take a message. Never give out a room number or say who is with the guest.
blocks.label: Safety

ul: **Log** every letter and parcel: date, time, for whom, from whom.
Store parcels safely behind the desk. For a guest who arrives tomorrow, note it on the booking.
For a guest who has left, follow the property's policy: forward it to the address left, or keep it safe for a set time.
Do not open a guest's mail, and do not leave parcels in public view.

blocks.p: A visitor who wants to go to a guest's room must wait in the lobby. **Phone the guest first**, and follow the guest's wishes. Never send a visitor upstairs on their own.

ul: Write the guest's **name, room number and time** on the wake-up call sheet and read it back. Use the 24-hour clock if the property does: 5:30 a.m. is 05:30, and 10:45 p.m. is 22:45.
Make the call at the time. If the guest does not answer, call again, then ask a colleague to knock on the door.
Record that the call was made, and by whom.

blocks.p: Guests may store valuables, such as jewellery, cash, passports and documents, in a safe deposit box at the front desk or in a safe in the room. Follow the procedure: the guest completes and **signs** the record, you note the box number and the time, you hold the key or the code as the policy says, and the guest signs again when taking the items out. Never open the box without the guest present. Never say what is inside, and never accept valuables without a record.

Answer within three rings if you can: 'Good afternoon, Cedar Hill Villa, Shanice speaking. How may I help you?' Speak slowly. Write down names and numbers. If you must put the caller on hold, ask first and thank them for waiting.

What reception tells them
What reception needs from them
rows: Housekeeping
Arrivals, departures, room changes, special requests, early arrivals
Which rooms are clean and inspected, lost property found
Maintenance
Faults reported by guests, with the room number and the time
When it will be fixed, and when the room is available again
Kitchen and restaurant
Special diets, birthdays, group meals, late arrivals
Opening times, menus, anything out of stock
Bell and security staff
Arrivals, luggage needs, suspicious people, lost keys
Reports of problems around the property
Accounts
Payments, deposits, disputed charges, cash and the float
Policies and decisions on credit and refunds

blocks.p: Good communication means the guest gets what was promised. Write messages down, pass them on clearly, and **follow up** to check they were done.

flow: Listen without interrupting
Say sorry and show you care
Find out the facts
Act, or pass it to the right person quickly
Tell the guest what will happen and when
Follow up and record it

blocks.p: Example: a guest complains that the air conditioner in their room does not work. Apologise, take the room number and details, report to maintenance at once, tell the guest when someone will come, and phone later to check it is fixed. If it cannot be fixed soon, offer another room if one is available. Record it in the log and the maintenance report.

ul: Stay calm. Do not take it personally. Never raise your voice.
Do not blame another department or person.
Do not promise what you cannot do. Say what you **can** do.
Refer big problems, such as a request for a refund or a compensation, to the supervisor.

head: Guest
How to help
rows: Poor eyesight
Read the registration form to them, offer to guide them, describe where things are, and tell them before you move something
Hard of hearing
Face the guest, speak clearly (do not shout), use writing, and make sure they know of fire alarm alternatives such as a flashing light or a knock
Wheelchair or walking difficulty
Give a ground-floor or accessible room, keep paths clear, and offer help without taking over
Elderly guest or a parent with a baby
Offer help with bags, a seat, a cot or a ground-floor room
Guest who does not speak English
Speak slowly, use simple words, a phrase card or a colleague who speaks the language

blocks.p: Always ask 'May I help you with that?' and wait for the answer. Treat the guest with respect, and talk to the guest, not only to the person with them.

flow: Greet the guest by name
Check and post any last charges
Print the bill (folio) for the guest to check
Answer or refer any query
Take payment and give a receipt
Collect the keys, return safe deposit items
Update room status and tell housekeeping
Thank the guest, and ask about their stay

ul: Ask about last charges: the restaurant, the minibar, laundry, phone and tours.
Let the guest read the bill. Explain every item. If the guest disagrees, check the record, and call the supervisor if needed. Never argue.
Collect all keys and key cards, and any property items the guest has borrowed, such as towels or beach chairs.
Check the safe deposit box and return the items against the guest's signature.
Tell the bell attendant if the guest needs help with luggage, and arrange transport if asked.

blocks.p: Many guests pay part in J$ and part in US$. Use **only the property's exchange rate for the day**, work out the sum on paper or the calculator, and show it to the guest. Give a receipt that shows each amount and its currency.

**Worked example (made-up figures for practice only).** A bill is US$520. The guest paid a deposit of US$200 on arrival, so the balance is US$320. The guest pays US$200 in cash and the rest in J$. The rest is US$120. The property's rate is US$1 = J$155, so 120 x 155 = **J$18,600**. The receipt shows US$200 and J$18,600, and the account is closed.

head: Late and early
Meaning
rows: Late check-out
The guest stays in the room after the normal check-out time, by agreement and sometimes for a fee
Early check-in
The guest receives the room before the normal check-in time
Express check-out
The guest leaves early or without waiting; the bill is emailed or left, and the card is charged as agreed
Skipper
A guest who leaves without paying; report to the manager at once

blocks.p: If the guest is leaving very early, before the desk opens, offer **express check-out**. At check-in, tell the guest and get their signed agreement to charge the card.

If a guest leaves something behind, take it to lost property, log it with the date, the room number and the finder's name, and try to contact the guest. Never use or give away guests' property. Keep it for the time the policy sets.

blocks.note: Cash refunds and credits need a supervisor's approval. Write every one in the log book and the folio.
blocks.label: Remember

ul: Never give out room numbers, names or dates of guests to callers or visitors.
Keep the registration cards, ID copies and card details out of sight and locked away. Lock your computer screen when you leave.
Report suspicious behaviour to security or your supervisor at once, for example a stranger trying door handles in the guest corridor. Do not confront them yourself.
Do not allow staff to take keys without signing for them.

blocks.p: Data protection law in Jamaica expects the property to look after guests' personal information and use it only for its proper purpose. Do not talk about a guest's details in public areas or on social media.
Reception holds the **in-house list**, the staff list and the visitors' book so that everyone can be counted. Learn the property's emergency plan and where the exits and the **assembly point** are.

flow: Stay calm; raise the alarm if you have not heard it
Call the fire service (110) or the police (119) if it is your duty
Take the in-house list, staff list and visitors' book (and master keys if the plan says)
Guide guests out by the stairs, not the lift
Help guests who need extra support
Do a roll call at the assembly point and report anyone missing
Let nobody back in until it is safe

blocks.note: In Jamaica, 119 is the number for the police, and 110 is the number for the ambulance and the fire service. Post these numbers beside the phone. Follow your property's own emergency plan.
blocks.label: Jamaica

blocks.h: The log book and the handover

ul: Write in the **front desk log book** the problems, requests, guests' complaints, keys issued or lost, and jobs still to be done.
At the end of the shift, give a **handover** to the next agent: arrivals still to come, rooms not ready, messages waiting, guests with problems, the float and cash, and any security issues.
Count the float again with your supervisor, and sign.
Never leave handover notes in view of guests.

A hold placed on the guest's card to cover the stay and extras
The fixed amount of cash a cashier starts the shift with
Whether a room is occupied, vacant dirty, vacant clean, inspected or out of order

c1.title: An early arrival in Port Antonio
c1.text: The Wilson family arrive at a villa property in Port Antonio at 10:30 a.m. They have a guaranteed booking for one room, and they have flown in from Atlanta overnight. Check-in time is 3 p.m. Housekeeping says the room they booked is 'vacant dirty' and will be ready at about 1 p.m. The father, Mr Trevor Wilson, is tired and a little impatient, and they have six pieces of luggage.

c2.title: A lost key card and a phone call
c2.text: At 9 p.m. a guest, Ms Joy Lindo, walks up to the desk and says she has lost her key card. She is wearing beach clothes and has no ID with her. At the same time, the phone rings: a man says he is her brother and asks which room she is in because he wants to surprise her. Agent Ricardo is alone at the desk. Another guest is waiting to ask about a taxi.

c3.title: A check-out with a mixed payment
c3.text: Mr Garfield Nunes checks out of a villa property after 6 nights. His bill is US$1,260. He paid US$300 on arrival. He wants to pay the balance with US$400 cash and the rest in J$. He also says the bill includes a minibar charge for two drinks that he did not have. For this question the property's rate is made up as US$1 = J$155. It is 6:30 a.m. and the desk has only just opened; a taxi is waiting.

c4.title: A guaranteed booking and a full house
c4.text: Miss Andrea Whyte arrives at 6 p.m. at a property in Mandeville with a guaranteed booking made through an agent. Every room is occupied because a guest has stayed extra nights, and nobody is leaving. The manager has just arrived on duty. A walk-in couple are also waiting, and the property has no rooms for them either.

c5.title: The evening shift in Negril
c5.text: On the evening shift at a villa property in Negril, agent Kimberly takes a request from Mr Hall for a wake-up call at 04:45 for a flight. A parcel arrives for a guest checking in next week. A guest, Mrs Samuels, asks to put her jewellery in the front desk safe deposit box. A loud noise in the corridor makes Kimberly look up, and she sees a stranger trying the handles of the doors on the first floor. The shift ends in an hour.

questions.q: When should Mr Wilson's family be allowed into the room?
o: When it is vacant clean and inspected, not before
As soon as housekeeping starts cleaning it, to save time
At once, because the booking is guaranteed and paid for
When the father agrees that the room is clean enough
questions.why: Only a room that has been cleaned and inspected may be given to a guest. A guarantee protects the booking, not the right to an unready room.

questions.q: What should the agent do while the family waits?
o: Ask them to leave and come back at 3 p.m. when the room is properly ready
Apologise, give an honest time, tag and store the bags, and finish registration
Give them any room that is empty, even if it is not yet cleaned or checked
Tell them the room will be ready soon, without a time, to avoid upsetting them
questions.why: Be honest about the time, make the wait comfortable, and do the paperwork in advance so the key is ready at once. Never promise what you cannot deliver.

questions.q: How should the luggage be handled?
o: Leave it by the desk, where the agent can see it from the front chair
Take it to the room that is being cleaned and leave it inside the door
Tag it and lock it away with the bell staff, giving the guest a stub
Ask the family to keep it with them in the lobby until the room is ready
questions.why: Luggage should be tagged and kept in a locked luggage room. Unattended bags in a lobby or an unfinished room are a security risk.

questions.q: Mr Wilson says, 'We want the room now.' Which reply is best?
o: The check-in time is 3 p.m., Mr Wilson, and it is the property's rule that all guests must wait until then
I will see what I can do, Mr Wilson, but the other guests came first so I cannot promise anything
You should have booked a later flight, Mr Wilson, as everyone knows rooms need cleaning first
I am sorry, Mr Wilson. It should be ready about 1 p.m., and I will call you at once
questions.why: Apologise, give a clear, honest time and promise a follow-up. Do not hide behind rules, blame the guest or give vague answers.

questions.q: Ms Lindo has lost her key card and has no ID. What should Ricardo do first?
o: Check her identity against the registration before making a key
Make a new key at once, because she is clearly a guest and wears beach clothes
Ask her to come back in the morning, when the manager is in the office
Tell her the room number aloud and ask her to say whether it is right
questions.why: A new key may be made only after the guest's identity is checked against the registration. This stops someone else from getting into the room.

questions.q: After the new key is made, what must happen to the lost card?
o: It is kept in a drawer until the guest finds it again
It is cancelled so that it can no longer open the door
It is reprogrammed to open the same door twice
Nothing, because a lost card cannot be used in the dark
questions.why: A cancelled card cannot open the door. Without cancelling, whoever finds it could enter the room.

questions.q: A man says he is Ms Lindo's brother and asks which room she is in. What should Ricardo say?
o: The room number, as he knows her name and says he is part of her family
That Ms Lindo is not staying here, so that the man cannot find her at all
That room numbers are private, but he can be put through or leave a message
The floor only, so that the man can go up and knock on the doors himself
questions.why: Never give out room numbers, or confirm who is staying. Offer to put the call through or take a message.

questions.q: Another guest is waiting for a taxi while Ricardo is busy. What is the best action?
o: Ignore the guest until the first job is done, as they can see that you are busy
Ask the guest to find a taxi in the street, because that is quicker for them
Ask the guest to come back later, when the lobby is quieter and you are free
Smile and say you will be there in a moment, then finish quickly
questions.why: Acknowledge waiting guests. A smile and a short word show them you know they are there, and prevent frustration.

questions.q: What is the balance Mr Nunes owes after his deposit?
He pays US$400 in cash and the rest in J$. How much is due in J$?
Mr Nunes disputes the minibar charge. What should the agent do?
o: Remove the charge at once, to avoid an argument at the desk in the morning
Tell him the bill is correct and that he must pay all of it before he leaves
Check the minibar record, and refer it to the supervisor if not settled
Ask him to pay now and write to the manager once he has left the property
questions.why: Check the record and be polite. If the query cannot be settled at once, refer it to the supervisor. Do not remove charges without authority or refuse to listen.

questions.q: What should the agent give Mr Nunes after payment?
o: A copy of the property's exchange rate sheet only
A note saying the account will be sent later
The key card to keep as a souvenir
A receipt showing each amount and its currency
questions.why: The receipt must show each payment and its currency, so the guest and the property have the same record.

questions.q: Miss Whyte has a guaranteed booking and no room is free. Who deals with this?
o: The manager, who arranges a room elsewhere
The agent, who offers her the room meant for the walk-in couple
The bell attendant, who finds a room by asking other guests to move
Reservations, who are asked to cancel her booking and refund her
questions.why: Walking a guest is a manager's decision. The property pays for the room at the other property and transport.

questions.q: What should the agent say to Miss Whyte?
o: Say it is the agent's fault and promise a free stay at some point in the future
Apologise and explain that the manager will arrange a room elsewhere
Tell her that bookings made through an agent are never really guaranteed
Say she should have phoned to confirm first, and that the property is not to blame
questions.why: Apologise and let the manager lead, using the policy. Blaming the guest or the agent harms the property's name.

questions.q: The walk-in couple ask for a room. What is the correct reply?
o: Offer them the room kept for Miss Whyte, since she is not yet checked in tonight
Ask them to wait in the lobby until someone leaves the next day or so
Explain politely that there is no room and suggest another property
Tell them that the property will be full for the whole of the year ahead
questions.why: If there is no room, say so politely, and offer help with another property. Never sell a room already promised to a guaranteed guest.

questions.q: For Mr Hall's 04:45 wake-up call, what should Kimberly record?
o: Only his name, because the time is easy to remember later
Only the room number, written on a sticky note on the phone
His flight number and the airline, in place of the wake-up time
His name, room and time, and read the request back to him
questions.why: Record name, room and time on the wake-up sheet, and read it back to check it. If he does not answer, call again, then send someone to knock.

questions.q: How should the parcel for next week's guest be handled?
o: Log it, store it safely and note it on the booking
Leave it on the desk until the guest comes in to collect it
Open it to see who sent it and what is inside it
Send it to the guest's room in advance with a bell attendant
questions.why: Parcels are logged and stored safely, with a note on the booking so the next shift knows. Never open them or leave them in public view.

questions.q: Mrs Samuels wants to put her jewellery in the safe deposit box. What should happen?
o: Take the jewellery in an envelope and put it in the desk drawer
Follow the procedure, with the guest signing the record
Ask her to keep it in the room, which the property says is safe
Tell her that the box is only used for passports and cash
questions.why: The safe deposit procedure needs a record signed by the guest. It protects both the guest and the property.

questions.q: What should Kimberly do about the stranger trying the door handles?
o: Walk up to him and tell him to leave, to show who is in charge here
Wait to see whether he gets into a room before doing anything about it
Report it at once to security or her supervisor, and do not confront him
Ignore it, because guests often try the wrong doors at night
questions.why: A person trying door handles may be a thief. Report at once to security or the supervisor and do not put yourself in danger.

questions.q: The shift is ending. What should Kimberly do about the jobs that are not finished?
o: Leave a note on the desk for any staff member who sees it
Finish them tomorrow, because the next agent will have enough work
Tell only the guests concerned, so they know who to ask
Write them in the log book and tell the next agent at handover
questions.why: A handover passes pending jobs, messages and problems to the next shift in writing and in person. Loose notes in view of guests are a security risk.
